title: How many are wrong?
fullTitle: Your Directory Has 10,000 Listings. How Many Are Wrong?

scenes.narration: Ten thousand listings. The number the directory is proud of, and the only one it has. A count says how many rows exist, not how many are right.
captions: 10,000 listings. The only number the directory has.
A count says how many rows exist, not how many are right.

scenes.narration: Behind the count sit several kinds of problem, and they overlap. One row can be a duplicate, carry a dead link, and hold an address nobody has confirmed in years. The dataset is synthetic and seeded: we know what was planted.
captions: Problems overlap: one row can carry several flags.
Synthetic, seeded dataset: we know exactly what was planted.

scenes.narration: Five checks run on the public rows only. Completeness. Duplicate candidates. URL syntax. Website availability, against a local mock responder, never real sites. And verification age, kept apart from last changed and last checked.
captions: Five checks on the public rows only. Website checks hit a local mock, not real sites.
Last verified is kept apart from last changed and last checked.

scenes.narration: The actual numbers. Three thousand eight hundred and seventy-five issue instances, but only three thousand three hundred and three distinct listings, because flags overlap. Add the columns together and you invent problems that do not exist.
captions: Adding the columns together invents problems that do not exist.

scenes.narration: Why a flag is not a verdict: Copper Framing's website timed out. In the ground truth, which the checker never saw, the business is open. Over a thousand failed website checks landed on open businesses.
captions: The website timed out. In the ground truth, the business is open.
1,038 failed website checks landed on open businesses.

scenes.narration: So uncertain cases are not deleted. They move into a review queue, each card carrying every reason it was flagged, ordered by what needs a human first.
captions: Uncertain cases go to a review queue, not the bin.
Each card carries every reason it was flagged.

scenes.narration: A reviewer records a decision with the evidence seen, a timestamp, and a name. Keep the listing, re-check in a week. Last checked moves. Last verified does not, because nothing was verified.
captions: A decision records evidence, timestamp and reviewer.
Last checked moves. Last verified does not.

scenes.narration: The checker also missed planted problems: moves with no edit trail, closed businesses whose sites still answer. A failed website check is a lead, not proof.
captions: The checker also missed planted problems. They are reported as missed.
A failed website check is a lead to investigate, not proof.
